question: A user asks Claude to build an interactive to-do list where items can be checked off and reordered directly in the browser. Which artifact type fits this request?
options: A) A CSV file listing each to-do item as a row, since CSV is the appropriate format whenever the user needs to track list items
B) An inline chat message with each item as a separate bullet, since inline lists let the user check items off directly in the conversation
C) A plain Markdown document artifact, since Markdown documents support checkboxes and are the standard format for to-do lists
D) An interactive React component artifact, since it supports the stateful, clickable interactions the to-do list requires
correct_answers: D) An interactive React component artifact, since it supports the stateful, clickable interactions the to-do list requires
explanations: Incorrect. CSV is a flat data format meant for tabular data exchange, not for delivering an interactive, clickable interface.
Incorrect. Inline chat text is static; a user cannot click to check off or reorder items directly within the conversation text.
Incorrect. A static Markdown document can show checkbox syntax but cannot support live reordering or interactive click behavior the way a component can.
Correct. React components are a supported artifact type built for interactive, stateful UI such as checking off and reordering items in the browser.
